issue.title: Speed up the CI pipeline

repository.name: netty
repository.description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework

issue.body:
I'm not sure if this is the best place to ask this kind of question. Have you thought about speeding up the current CI pipeline? It looks like that it takes [about an hour and a half](https://garage.netty.io/teamcity/viewLog.html?buildId=22194&buildTypeId=pulls_netty&guest=1) to build the project and run all tests.

Have you thought about running your unit-tests in parallel? If I'm not mistaken, Maven can run JUnit tests in parallel via the [surefire plugin](https://maven.apache.org/surefire/maven-surefire-plugin/examples/fork-options-and-parallel-execution.html).

Or maybe migrating to [Gradle](https://gradle.org/) would be a good idea to improve the performance of the project's builds? Gradle [claims](https://gradle.org/gradle-vs-maven-performance/) that it's much faster than Maven on different types of projects, can compile your project using [incremental compilation](https://guides.gradle.org/performance/#incremental_compilation), run your [tests in parallel](https://guides.gradle.org/performance/#parallel_test_execution) and much more. 

I'm not quite sure if this is a problem right now (slow CI builds), but maybe it could save you some time in the long run and increase the overall responsiveness. WDYT?
